candidates.name: sys — System-specific parameters and functions
verified_facts: Exposes interpreter identity and runtime attributes including executable, version information, prefixes, arguments, and module search state.
semantic_limits: Interpreter attributes alone do not prove the process is the canonical F-host runner or that a receipt is valid.

candidates.name: The initialization of the sys.path module search path
verified_facts: Documents how the executable, environment variables, landmarks, virtual environments, and site processing initialize sys.path.
semantic_limits: A plausible sys.path does not prove imported modules came from the intended files without origin and hash correlation.

candidates.name: venv — Creation of virtual environments
verified_facts: Virtual environments separate sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix from base_prefix and base_exec_prefix.
semantic_limits: Activation state or prefix differences do not prove dependency integrity or canonical task ownership.

candidates.name: site — Site-specific configuration hook
verified_facts: Processes site-packages paths and path configuration files during interpreter initialization unless disabled.
semantic_limits: Site processing can alter import paths, so path entries require origin and file-hash validation.

candidates.name: sysconfig — Python configuration information
verified_facts: Exposes installation schemes, configuration variables, and standard library path locations.
semantic_limits: Configuration variables describe the interpreter build but do not prove the active executable or packages are untampered.

candidates.name: platform — Access to underlying platform identifying data
verified_facts: Provides system, release, machine, architecture, and Python implementation identification helpers.
semantic_limits: Platform strings may be incomplete or normalized and cannot replace executable, process, and OS evidence.

candidates.name: importlib — The implementation of import
verified_facts: Defines import machinery, module specifications, loaders, and cache invalidation behavior.
semantic_limits: A successful import does not prove the module origin or content without spec, path, and hash readback.

candidates.name: importlib.metadata — Accessing package metadata
verified_facts: Provides distribution version, metadata, files, requirements, and entry-point discovery from installed packages.
semantic_limits: Package metadata can be stale or incomplete and must be correlated with actual files and interpreter paths.

candidates.name: importlib.resources — Package resource reading, opening and access
verified_facts: Provides Traversable-based access to resources within importable packages without assuming a persistent filesystem path.
semantic_limits: Resource access does not prove package authenticity or that resources belong to the canonical task.

candidates.name: pkgutil — Package extension utility
verified_facts: Supports module discovery, package walking, loader lookup, and package data access.
semantic_limits: Discovery results depend on current import paths and do not establish module provenance or integrity.

candidates.name: inspect — Inspect live objects
verified_facts: Provides live-object inspection, source-file lookup, signatures, stack frames, and coroutine or generator state.
semantic_limits: Introspection can fail for built-ins or transformed code and does not authenticate the inspected object.

candidates.name: gc — Garbage Collector interface
verified_facts: Exposes garbage-collector enablement, thresholds, statistics, tracked objects, and explicit collection.
semantic_limits: GC state can explain memory behavior but does not prove task completion or receipt persistence.

candidates.name: pathlib — Object-oriented filesystem paths
verified_facts: Provides path resolution, stat, ownership, link, directory, and file operations through concrete path objects.
semantic_limits: String equality between paths does not prove the same final file; handle, stat, and hash correlation remain required.
